10.t: Working with data: surfactant and premature babies
q: Describe the relationship between length of pregnancy and breathing difficulties.
The longer the pregnancy, the fewer difficulties: 90 per 100 at 26 weeks falling to 1 at 39 weeks.
Explain this relationship using type II pneumocytes.

Type II pneumocytes make surfactant mainly in late pregnancy. Surfactant lowers surface tension in the fluid lining the alveoli, so they do not collapse and are easier to inflate. Early babies have too little.
Calculate the percentage reduction in difficulties at 30 weeks when steroids are given.
Suggest how steroids given to the mother reduce breathing difficulties.
The steroid crosses the placenta, enters the baby’s lung cells and switches on genes that speed up surfactant production.
Suggest why steroids make almost no difference from 36 weeks.
The lungs are already making enough surfactant.
